adventure.title: Kayak Moriches Bay from Remsenburg
adventure.description: Launch into the quiet flats of Moriches Bay right off Remsenburg and paddle the marsh channels toward the Moriches Inlet barrier beach.
adventure.bonus: Reach a sandbar only accessible by boat and stand on land no car can reach.

adventure.title: Wertheim National Wildlife Refuge, Shirley
adventure.description: The Carmans River refuge minutes west of Remsenburg — paddle the tidal river or hike the Black Tupelo and White Oak trails through untouched estuary.
adventure.bonus: Paddle the Carmans upriver until the saltwater turns fresh, then drift back down.

adventure.title: Elizabeth Morton National Wildlife Refuge
adventure.description: The 187-acre Noyac refuge with a beach on Peconic Bay is one of the last undeveloped shorelines on the South Fork — shorebirds, horseshoe crabs in June, and the bay to yourself.
adventure.bonus: Get there at low tide and walk the full beach shoreline.

adventure.title: Long Island Wine Trail — North Fork Loop
adventure.description: Cross Peconic Bay to the North Fork and spend a day hitting five or six of the 60+ vineyards along the North Fork Wine Trail — Bedell, Channing Daughters, Shinn Estate — the Bordeaux varietals are the story.
adventure.bonus: Pick three wineries max and spend a full hour at each one.

adventure.title: Montauk Point Lighthouse Hike
adventure.description: The 1796 lighthouse at the eastern tip of Long Island sits on bluffs above the rocky point where the Sound meets the Atlantic — climb the 137 steps to the light and see all the way to Block Island.
adventure.bonus: Climb to the light and stay at the top until you can name every direction you're looking.

adventure.title: Hither Hills State Park Camping
adventure.description: The campground between the ocean and Napeague Harbor is the only way to actually sleep in Montauk for under $100 — the walking dunes, the harbor kayaking, and the surf fishing are all from your campsite.
adventure.bonus: Book the ocean-side sites — wake up to the surf 200 yards from your tent.

adventure.title: Camp Hero State Park Explore
adventure.description: The decommissioned Cold War military base at the end of Montauk has bunkers in the dunes, an abandoned SAGE radar installation, bluefish running off the rocks, and the most unusual landscape in New York.
adventure.bonus: Find the radar dish on the hillside and walk around the full perimeter fence.

adventure.title: Georgica Pond Kayak at Sunset
adventure.description: The freshwater pond behind the East Hampton barrier beach is kayakable at high summer — put in from the town beach access and paddle the pond edge as the light drops over the dunes.
adventure.bonus: Paddle to the ocean-side beach access and watch the surf from the dune top.

adventure.title: Stand-Up Paddleboard Sagg Pond to the Atlantic
adventure.description: Sagaponack's hidden pond connects to the ocean through a narrow channel that delivers a genuinely wild open-water moment.
adventure.bonus: Cross the sandbar channel into open Atlantic water on your board — if a wave knocks you off, you have to swim the board back before remounting.

adventure.title: Cliff Scramble at Shadmoor State Park
adventure.description: Montauk's bluff trails drop you onto a wild, boulder-strewn beach that feels nothing like the manicured Hamptons everyone else visits.
adventure.bonus: Scramble down to the beach without using the main path — find the unofficial bluff descent and make it down without using your hands.

adventure.title: Kayak the Mashomack Preserve on Shelter Island
adventure.description: 2,000 acres of tidal creeks and osprey-dotted marshland make this the most underrated paddle in the Hamptons ecosystem.
adventure.bonus: Navigate into one tidal creek so narrow the reeds brush both sides of your kayak — if you can touch the shore without tipping, it counts.

adventure.title: Sunrise Surf at Ditch Plains Beach
adventure.description: Montauk's most beloved break delivers consistent waves at dawn when the crowds are gone and the Atlantic turns gold.
adventure.bonus: Catch a wave, ride it all the way to shore, and then go back out immediately — no celebrating on the beach until you've done it twice.

social.title: Tide Runners, Hampton Bays
social.description: The waterfront bar and grill on the Shinnecock Canal where boats pull straight up to the dock for a drink — pure summer canal scene.
social.bonus: Get a dock table and watch at least three boats tie up for dinner.

social.title: Canoe Place Inn, Hampton Bays
social.description: The historic 1920s roadhouse on the canal, reborn as a waterfront inn and event venue — the western gateway to the Hamptons since the steamship era.
social.bonus: Have a cocktail on the canal-side terrace and find out what the building used to be.

social.title: Neptune Beach Club, Hampton Bays
social.description: The Dune Road beach club that runs from daytime bottle-service sand straight into a packed night party on Shinnecock Bay.
social.bonus: Stay through the daytime-to-nighttime flip without leaving the property.

social.title: The Boardy Barn, Hampton Bays
social.description: The legendary Sunday-only afternoon party in Hampton Bays — happy-sticker chaos, a brass band, and an institution since 1969. Summer Sundays only.
social.bonus: Earn a happy-face sticker from a stranger before you earn your first beer.

social.title: 75 Main Southampton Late Night
social.description: The Main Street Southampton supper club that turns into the Hamptons' social scene after 11pm — the dinner is fine, the crowd after midnight is the whole reason anyone stays that late.
social.bonus: Don't arrive before 10:30pm — the room doesn't exist before then.

social.title: Pierre's Bistro Bridgehampton
social.description: The French bistro on Montauk Highway in Bridgehampton where the regulars eat three nights a week and the bar fills with people who've been arguing about the same things since Memorial Day.
social.bonus: Sit at the bar and let the room come to you.

social.title: Montauk Brewing Company Taproom
social.description: The Montauk Brewing taproom on South Erie Street is the local's escape from the resort bars — the Summer Ale and the Wave Chaser IPA are both made here, and the patio is unpretentious.
social.bonus: Order a flight of everything on tap before picking a pint.

social.title: Gurney's Montauk Pool Bar Day
social.description: The Gurney's resort sits on the Montauk bluffs with an oceanfront pool and a bar that charges resort prices for the view — one day pass, one afternoon, worth every dollar of it.
social.bonus: Book a beach chair at the water's edge and stay until the bar closes.

social.title: Stephen Talkhouse Live Show, Amagansett
social.description: The tiny Amagansett music venue has hosted Billy Joel, Paul McCartney, and every band that's ever summered here — 100 capacity, incredible sound, and a summer calendar that never disappoints.
social.bonus: Get as close to the stage as possible and don't move.

social.title: American Hotel Bar, Sag Harbor
social.description: The 1846 hotel bar in Sag Harbor village has the best wine list east of the city and a mahogany bar that's been in continuous use since before the Hamptons were called the Hamptons.
social.bonus: Order a bottle from the cellar, not the by-the-glass list — the cellar is the real reason to come.

social.title: Late Night at Surf Lodge Montauk
social.description: Montauk's most famous venue plants you barefoot in the sand at a live music night that runs from acoustic sets to full-on dance floor without breaking a sweat.
social.bonus: Dance on the sand directly in front of the stage for at least one full song — no phone out, no self-consciousness, all in.

social.title: Happy Hour on the Dock at The Harbor Bar at Baron's Cove
social.description: Sag Harbor's most social dock bar puts you directly over the water at golden hour with the entire marina as your backdrop.
social.bonus: Challenge a stranger at the bar to a game of liar's dice — loser buys the next round.

social.title: Sunday Brunch at Tutto Il Giorno
social.description: Sag Harbor's waterfront Italian brings a downtown Manhattan crowd to a Peconic Bay terrace where the people-watching is as good as the tagliolini.
social.bonus: Start a conversation with the table next to you by asking them to recommend one dish — stay in conversation long enough to actually order it.

active.title: Sears-Bellows County Park Trails, Hampton Bays
active.description: Pine-barrens trails around a chain of freshwater ponds just north of Hampton Bays — hiking, a swimming pond, and almost no one there.
active.bonus: Hike the loop around Sears Pond and swim before anyone else arrives.

active.title: Shinnecock Canal Kayak, Hampton Bays
active.description: Paddle the canal that links Shinnecock Bay to the Peconic — time it with the lock current and you barely have to paddle one direction.
active.bonus: Launch on the outgoing current and let it carry you toward the bay.

active.title: Cupsogue Beach County Park
active.description: The wild western tip of the barrier island past Westhampton — tidal flats, kayaking, and a clamming-and-seal-watching scene the East End never sees.
active.bonus: Wade out to the sand flats at low tide and walk as far as the water lets you.

active.title: Dune Road Bike Ride, Westhampton Beach
active.description: The flat barrier-beach road with the ocean on one side and the bay on the other — the definitive western Hamptons ride.
active.bonus: Ride east until the pavement narrows, then turn around and race your own time back.

active.title: Coopers Beach to Meadow Lane Bike Ride
active.description: Bike Meadow Lane in Southampton between the ocean and Lake Agawam — the road is flanked by the most expensive real estate in America on one side and an open bay on the other. 6am, no traffic.
active.bonus: Count the houses you'd buy if money didn't matter.

active.title: Ditch Plains Surfing, Montauk
active.description: The rocky point beach west of Montauk village breaks consistently and has been the East End surf scene since the '60s — rent a board from Pilgrim Surf + Supply and paddle out.
active.bonus: Stay in the water until you catch a wave all the way to the sand.

active.title: Napeague Walking Dunes Hike
active.description: The parabolic dunes in Napeague between Amagansett and Montauk shift 3 feet a year and bury trees from below — the 3-mile loop through the dunes is the strangest landscape in New York.
active.bonus: Climb the highest dune and sit on top until you spot the harbor through the trees.

active.title: Springs Fireplace Road Running Trail
active.description: The back-country roads of Springs, the artists' neighborhood of East Hampton, make the best morning run in the Hamptons — no traffic, Accabonac Harbor visible through the trees, Pollock's old neighborhood.
active.bonus: Run to Louse Point and back for the harbor view at the turnaround.

active.title: Paddleboard Lake Agawam, Southampton
active.description: The freshwater lake in the middle of Southampton village is paddleboardable on calm mornings — the waterside mansions on one bank, the village park on the other, and total silence.
active.bonus: Paddle the full perimeter of the lake without stopping.

active.title: Sag Harbor Village Waterfront Bike Loop
active.description: Bike the Sag Harbor village streets, the harbor waterfront, and the Eastville neighborhood loop — 5 miles of flat, the whaling-era architecture around every corner.
active.bonus: Find the oldest house in the village — the historical society marker is on the door.

active.title: Kayak Accabonac Harbor, Springs
active.description: The tidal harbor behind Springs empties into Gardiner's Bay — kayak the marsh channel at high tide past the osprey platforms and the salt marshes that the East Hampton artists painted for a hundred years.
active.bonus: Paddle out to the bay mouth and look back at the harbor from the open water.

active.title: Surf Fishing Montauk Point at Dawn
active.description: The rocks below the Montauk lighthouse at dawn are where the striped bass and bluefish run in fall — local surf casters have been here before sunrise, and the rips off the point are legendary.
active.bonus: Talk to whoever was there before you — they know the spot.

active.title: Tennis at Sportime Amagansett
active.description: Book an early court at the East End's best outdoor tennis facility and play a set while the dew is still on the surface and the day belongs to you.
active.bonus: Challenge a stranger warming up on the next court to a tiebreaker set — winner owes nothing, loser buys the post-match coffee.

active.title: Open-Water Swim at Two Mile Hollow Beach
active.description: East Hampton's locals-only stretch of coastline is where serious swimmers do their open-water training in some of the cleanest Atlantic water on Long Island.
active.bonus: Swim parallel to shore past three lifeguard stands without stopping — if the current runs against you, it counts double.

active.title: Bike the Poxabogue Greenway to Wainscott
active.description: The back-road bike route from Bridgehampton through Poxabogue pond to Wainscott Beach is the flattest, most satisfying 10-mile ride on the East End.
active.bonus: Complete the entire route without unclipping — no stopping, no foot on ground — and swim in the ocean at the finish as your reward.

chill.title: Ponquogue Beach, Hampton Bays
chill.description: The locals' ocean beach in Hampton Bays beneath the old bridge — surfers, fishermen and far fewer crowds than the East End.
chill.bonus: Walk from the lot to the bridge pilings and back along the waterline.

chill.title: Westhampton Beach Performing Arts Center
chill.description: The restored 1930s theater on Main Street that anchors WHB's cultural scene — music, comedy and film a short drive from Remsenburg.
chill.bonus: Buy a ticket to whatever is playing tonight without looking up the act first.

chill.title: Rogers Beach, Westhampton Beach
chill.description: The main ocean beach for Westhampton Beach village — wide, pavilioned, and the easiest stretch of Atlantic to reach from Remsenburg.
chill.bonus: Stay until the lifeguards leave and you have the sand to yourself.

chill.title: Quogue Wildlife Refuge
chill.description: A 305-acre preserve of trails, ponds and a nature center with resident owls and hawks — the quietest place in the western Hamptons.
chill.bonus: Walk the full pond loop without checking your phone once.

chill.title: Pollock-Krasner House, Springs
chill.description: Jackson Pollock's farmhouse in Springs, East Hampton — the barn studio still has the paint drips on the floor from the years he invented Abstract Expressionism here. One of the most important art sites in America.
chill.bonus: Stand in the barn studio and look at the floor — that's where the drip paintings happened.

chill.title: Main Beach East Hampton Morning
chill.description: The voted-best-beach-in-America multiple times — at 7am it's empty, the sand is immaculate, the lifeguard stands aren't up yet, and the Atlantic is the only thing ahead of you.
chill.bonus: Swim before anyone else arrives — the beach belongs to you for about 45 minutes.

chill.title: Quail Hill Farm Montauk Highway
chill.description: The organic community farm in Amagansett runs a farmstand and U-pick operation from June through October — the farm fields between the highway and the ocean are what the Hamptons looked like before the houses arrived.
chill.bonus: Pick your own vegetables and cook them that night.

chill.title: Peconic Bay Sunset Cruise from Greenport
chill.description: The evening sailing cruises on Peconic Bay out of Greenport put you on the water between the North and South Forks as the sun drops — the bay turns pink and the North Fork vineyards glow on the left bank.
chill.bonus: Bring a bottle of Wölffer rosé on board — most cruises allow it.

chill.title: Sag Harbor Whaling Museum & Village Walk
chill.description: The 1845 Greek Revival mansion that houses the whaling museum anchors a village that was more important than Manhattan in 1850 — the Federal-style streetscape is the best-preserved in New York.
chill.bonus: Walk the full village grid before entering the museum.

chill.title: Montauk Village Morning Coffee Loop
chill.description: Montauk village at 7am — the surfers are already in the water, the bait shop is open, and the diner has been serving the same egg sandwich since the '70s. The village at its most itself.
chill.bonus: Eat at the counter of the diner, not a booth.

chill.title: Guild Hall East Hampton Gallery
chill.description: The East Hampton arts institution on Main Street has been showing the work of East End artists since 1931 — the summer exhibition program runs through October and always has at least one thing that stops you.
chill.bonus: Buy one piece from the artist shop before you leave.

chill.title: Wine and Twilight at Wölffer Estate Vineyard
chill.description: Sagaponack's most beautiful vineyard pours estate rosé on a terrace overlooking rows of vines as the light goes amber — this is what summer in the Hamptons actually looks like.
chill.bonus: Ask the sommelier to pour you something you can't pronounce — then guess the grape variety before they tell you.

chill.title: Afternoon at Parrish Art Museum
chill.description: Water Mill's Herzog & de Meuron barn holds one of the great collections of East End art in an airy, honest building that matches its landscape.
chill.bonus: Find the single work in the collection that moves you most, sit in front of it for ten uninterrupted minutes, and write one sentence about why.

chill.title: Sunset at Camp Hero State Park Bluffs
chill.description: Montauk's decommissioned radar station sits on cliffs above the Atlantic with unobstructed 180-degree sunsets that routinely stop traffic.
chill.bonus: Put your phone away for the entire duration of sunset — not airplane mode, fully in your bag — and just watch it go down.

chill.title: Read at the East Hampton Library Garden
chill.description: A hidden courtyard garden behind one of the most beautiful public libraries on the East Coast delivers total stillness two blocks from Main Street.
chill.bonus: Pick a book off the shelf you know nothing about, sit in the garden, and commit to reading the first 50 pages before you leave.

foodie.title: Oakland's Restaurant & Marina, Hampton Bays
foodie.description: Right at the Shinnecock Inlet where the bay meets the ocean — lobster, a sand-floor tiki bar, and the best inlet sunset in the Hamptons.
foodie.bonus: Order the lobster, then move to the tiki bar for the actual sunset.

foodie.title: Westhampton Bake Shoppe
foodie.description: The Main Street bakery famous for its black-and-white cookies and crumb-topped everything — the morning line is the WHB social hour.
foodie.bonus: Buy one black-and-white cookie and eat it walking down Main Street, no plate.

foodie.title: Cowfish, Hampton Bays
foodie.description: The Shinnecock Canal hotspot with a sushi-meets-raw-bar menu and a deck right on the water where the boats tie up.
foodie.bonus: Get a seat on the water side and watch a boat dock for dinner while you eat.

foodie.title: Eckart's Luncheonette, Quogue
foodie.description: The tiny Quogue breakfast counter that locals have been crowding into for generations — eggs, pancakes, zero pretension, cash-friendly.
foodie.bonus: Sit at the counter and order whatever the regular next to you is having.

foodie.title: Dockers Waterside, East Quogue
foodie.description: The Shinnecock Bay waterfront restaurant where the entire western Hamptons turns up for the sunset — get there before the sun drops or you'll miss the whole point.
foodie.bonus: Be seated on the deck a full hour before sunset and order the raw bar while you wait.

foodie.title: Starr Boggs, Westhampton Beach
foodie.description: The white-tablecloth seafood room that has defined Westhampton Beach dining for decades — local fish, a famous Thursday lobster bake, and a garden out back.
foodie.bonus: Order the whole local fish of the day and let the table split it family-style.

foodie.title: Sant Ambroeus Southampton Terrace
foodie.description: The Milan-style coffee bar on Job's Lane does the best espresso in the Hamptons — the terrace scene on a Saturday morning is the entire social scene of Southampton compressed into one block.
foodie.bonus: Order a Bicerin and read whatever you brought without talking to anyone for an hour.

foodie.title: The Lobster Roll (LUNCH) on the Highway
foodie.description: The roadside seafood shack in Napeague between Amagansett and Montauk that has been serving the cold mayo lobster roll since 1965 — the sign says LUNCH because the owner's wife's name is Lunch.
foodie.bonus: Eat it at the picnic table outside and order a second one before finishing the first.

foodie.title: Topping Rose House Farm Dinner
foodie.description: Tom Colicchio's Bridgehampton restaurant on the Topping Rose estate uses the on-site farm for the menu — the farm-to-table pitch is actually true here, and the terrace has the best view in Bridgehampton.
foodie.bonus: Order the farm vegetable plate whatever it is that night — don't skip it for protein.

foodie.title: Duryea's Lobster Deck, Montauk
foodie.description: The lobster pound on Fort Pond Bay that got famous before it had a sign — whole lobsters, drawn butter, chilled rosé, picnic tables on the bay. Book weeks ahead or show up at 5pm and wait.
foodie.bonus: Order the full lobster, not the roll — crack it yourself.

foodie.title: La Fondita Tacos, East Hampton
foodie.description: The walk-up taco window in the back of a parking lot on Newtown Lane — the best taco in the Hamptons costs $4 and has a longer line than any restaurant on Main Street.
foodie.bonus: Order at least five — you'll regret ordering fewer.

foodie.title: Sen Japanese, Southampton Village
foodie.description: The Japanese restaurant in the village has held its reputation quietly for years — the omakase-style ordering approach gets you into territory that most Southampton visitors never find.
foodie.bonus: Let the chef choose every dish — don't look at the menu at all.

foodie.title: Scoop du Jour Ice Cream, Southampton
foodie.description: The small-batch ice cream shop on Hampton Road has been the after-dinner tradition for Southampton locals for years — the seasonal flavors change weekly and the waffle cone is mandatory.
foodie.bonus: Order whatever seasonal flavor you can't identify by name alone.

foodie.title: Sag Harbor Provisions Market Picnic
foodie.description: The Sag Harbor village market makes the sandwiches and salads that end up on the harbor waterfront — build a picnic, walk to the wharf, eat looking at the boats.
foodie.bonus: Buy enough for two people even if you're alone.

foodie.title: Nick & Toni's East Hampton
foodie.description: The 35-year-old East Hampton institution where everyone who's been coming to the Hamptons longer than you has a regular table — wood-fired Tuscan cooking, local produce, the best pasta east of the city.
foodie.bonus: Ask for a table by the fireplace even in summer — the room is better from that side.

foodie.title: Early Breakfast at Candy Kitchen
foodie.description: Bridgehampton's Greek-diner time capsule has served the same chrome-counter breakfast since 1956 — eggs, coffee, and zero pretension.
foodie.bonus: Sit at the counter, order off-menu by describing exactly what you want — if they make it without hesitation, you've found a local.

foodie.title: Farm Stand Crawl on Sagg Main Street
foodie.description: Sagaponack's single-lane farm road is lined with honor-system stands selling just-picked corn, tomatoes, and flowers that redefine what produce should taste like.
foodie.bonus: Buy something from every stand you pass without spending more than $20 total — then build a meal from what you've collected.

foodie.title: Tasting Menu at Calissa
foodie.description: Water Mill's upscale Greek taverna plates whole branzino and proper loukoumades in a whitewashed setting that earns every dollar of its price tag.
foodie.bonus: Order a dish entirely in Greek — ask your server what it's called and pronounce it back to them before they put in the order.
